title: Slice Synthesis Governance and Localization Playbook
author: Maya Singh
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the governance process and technical procedure for synthesizing evaluation slices and localized derivative probes used in continuous evals, stress benchmarks, and production shadowing. It defines responsibilities, sampling budgets, quality gates, telemetry contracts, and localization constraints to ensure probes remain representative and safe across languages, regions, and product features.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers
- Evaluator / probe authors
- Product QA and Safety stewards
- Model-onboarding owners

Scope:
This document covers:
- Derivative probe generation (seed mutation, paraphrase, noise injection).
- Cross-locale and dialect localization rules.
- Sampling governance (budgets, quotas, retention).
- Telemetry and metadata contract for probes and synthetic examples.
- Quality guardrails and automatic rejection criteria.
Not in scope: human annotation instructions (see related annotation charters) and private customer data handling (see privacy-first-shadow-eval-and-dp-certification).

Definitions:
- Seed: a canonical prompt or user-exemplar used to generate derivative probes.
- Derivative probe: any synthetic or transformed prompt created from a seed (paraphrase, translation, noise-perturbed, adapter-context).
- Slice: a labeled subset of workload defined by intent, complexity, or locale (e.g., billing-clarification, spanish-colloquial, long-context).
- Localization family: group of locales/languages sharing a translation and cultural adaptation policy (e.g., en-US/en-GB -> English family).

Governance principles:
1) Traceability: Every derivative probe must include provenance metadata: seed_id, generator_version, transformation_chain, author, and creation_timestamp.
2) Minimal human cost: Favor automatic synthesis when quality gates pass; preserve human review for high-risk slices or customer-impacting features.
3) Budgeted sampling: Each team has a monthly synthesis budget in tokens and probe-counts; budget exhausted => escalation to evaluator lead.
4) Local fidelity: For localization families, include at least one native-speaker validation sample per slice for languages with >1% of traffic.

Metadata (telemetry) contract (required fields):
- probe_id (string)
- seed_id (string)
- slice_tags (list)
- generator (string) e.g. "paraphrase-v2" or "translate-bridge-en-to-es"
- generator_version (string)
- transform_chain (string) e.g. "seed->synonym-perturb(0.2)->paraphrase-v2"
- locale (string) e.g. "es-419"
- estimated_token_cost (int)
- human_review_status (enum) {none, sampled, approved, rejected}
- provenance_url (string) link to source artifact in eval-mesh or storage
- safety_review_tag (string) optional safety label if flagged

Sampling and budget rules:
- Default budget per owning team: 5k probes / month or 1M tokens, whichever is first.
- High-risk slices (financial instructions, legal guidance) capped at 500 auto-synth probes / month unless human-reviewed.
- Localization multiplier: for locales marked as "high fidelity" (top 10% traffic), synthesize a 1:1 ratio to en seeds; for low-traffic locales, cap at 10% of en volume.
- Retention policy: keep synthesized probes and metadata for 24 months. Older probes must be archived with audit trail.

Quality gates (automated):
Run in order; failure at any gate marks the probe as "rejected-automated" and triggers triage.
1) Tokenization sanity: probe must tokenize without OOV errors and token count <= 4x seed length.
2) Semantic-presence check: intent classifier confidence >= 0.7 for target slice.
3) Toxicity filter: run safety classifier v3; toxicity score < 0.2 or flagged for human_review_status.
4) Model-consistency smoke: run lightweight evaluator (evaluator-lite) against production model and baseline model: normalized response similarity >= 0.65 (unless slice expects diversity).
5) Locale fluency spot-check: language identification must match locale with confidence >= 0.9.

Quality gates (human):
- Any probe failing automated gates but within salvage thresholds (e.g., toxicity between 0.2-0.35) is queued for human review.
- Human review checklist: fluency, cultural appropriateness, PII leakage, and instruction preservation. Use the HumanReview UI in eval-mesh (link in related_pages).

Derivation strategies (examples):
- Paraphrase ensemble: 3 paraphrase models (paraphrase-v1/v2/paraphrase-light) with disagreement pruning: keep probes where at least 2 models agree on intent classifier.
- Translation bridge: seed->translate(en->pivot_lang)->paraphrase->back-translate->normalize. Include intermediate artifacts for audit.
- Noise injection: controlled character/token-level perturbations to simulate ASR/typo errors; parameterize by noise_rate (0.01, 0.05, 0.1).

Procedure: Creating a new localized slice (step-by-step)
1) Define slice in the slice registry: slug, owner_team, acceptance_criteria, and initial seed list (minimum 20 seeds).
2) Create a synthesis job in probe-orch with parameters: generator_set, locale_targets, noise_profile, and sampling_budget. Example CLI: 
   probe-orch create --slice billing-clarification --seeds seeds/billing-clarity-2025.json --generators paraphrase-v2,translate-bridge --locales en-US,es-419 --budget 200
3) Probe-orch emits artifacts to s3://eval-mesh/synth/{slice}/{job_id}/ including metadata.json and samples.csv.
4) Run auto-gates: call eval-harness auto-gate --input s3://eval-mesh/synth/{job_id}/metadata.json --out s3://eval-mesh/synth/{job_id}/gated.json
5) If any probes are queued for human review, assign to a reviewer via the HumanReview UI and mark status.
6) Approve and promote a subset (minimum 200 approved probes) to the probe registry for continuous evals.

Role and ownership matrix:
- Slice owner: owns definition, acceptance criteria, and seed list. (Team-level)
- Probe author: initiates synthesis jobs and triage. (Applied ML / Evaluator)
- Quality steward: signs off on human-reviewed probes for high-risk slices. (Safety / Product)
- Telemetry owner: ensures probes emit required metadata. (Observability / Eng-DE)

Metrics and SLOs for synthesis pipeline:
- Gate processing latency: 95th percentile <= 2 minutes per probe for automated gates.
- Human review turnaround: median <= 48 hours for sampled probes.
- Rejection rate (automated): target < 12% for low-risk slices; < 6% for seeded QA sets.
- Localization coverage: top-10 locales must reach 95% of planned probe volume within 7 days of job completion.

Example metadata JSON (single-line, stored in metadata.json):
{"probe_id":"probe-20260115-0001","seed_id":"seed-billing-0007","slice_tags":["billing","clarification","long-context"],"generator":"paraphrase-v2","generator_version":"2.1.0","transform_chain":"seed->paraphrase-v2->noise(0.01)","locale":"es-419","estimated_token_cost":18,"human_review_status":"none","provenance_url":"s3://eval-mesh/synth/billing-20260115/job-7/probe-0001.txt"}

Interoperability notes (integration with quantization profiles and runtime):
- Mark probes with a "quant_sensitivity" tag when probes exercise long-context or high-precision numeric outputs. This flag must trigger the quant-impact-synthesis pipeline (see quantization-profiles directory) to validate behavior under int8/int4 artifacts.
- For probes in dedicated/private workloads, ensure the provenance_url points to private storage and that telemetry respects customer-data redaction policies.

Triage playbook for regression signals (quick steps):
1) Alert from evaluation-dashboard identifies a slice-level quality drop > 5% compared to baseline.
2) Kick off synthetic-bisect: re-run the slice with multiple random seeds and generator_versions to determine whether regression is generator- or model-driven.
3) Check derivation metadata for generator_version drift or locale mapping changes.
4) If candidate root cause is quant-related, add quant-sensitivity-tagged probes to the failing cohort and re-evaluate under quantized artifacts.
5) If human-safety issue found, escalate to Safety oncall and freeze synthetic generation for affected slice.

Rollout and deprecation policy:
- New slice must run in shadow for 2 weeks with continuous monitoring and a minimum of 1k interactions.
- Deprecate a slice only after: owner_team sign-off, archival of artifacts, and update to slice registry.

Appendix: example slice registry table (column descriptions)
- slug: short identifier for the slice (string)
- owner: Owning team
- seeds_count: initial seed count
- target_locales: comma-separated locale list
- risk_level: low|medium|high
- last_audit: YYYY-MM-DD
